issues.description: ACL.root field complects 'is-root-policy' with 'which namespace owns it'
issues.detail: The bool became a *Namespace pointer that simultaneously encodes presence, ownership, and ancestry scope. Three facts ride on one field: 'this ACL has root caps,' 'rooted at this namespace,' 'check ancestry on each call.' A small value type like RootScope{Owner *Namespace} or a separate root bool plus owner field would separate the presence-check from the scope-check and stop readers from grepping nil-vs-non-nil to infer policy.

issues.description: NamespaceSealed stub returns false silently — identity and time of 'sealed' are undefined
issues.detail: The method's contract claims 'direct ancestry line' but implementation returns false unconditionally with a TODO. Callers (ListAllNamespaces, etc.) now branch on a value with no time semantics: what 'sealed' means, when it changes, and who observes the transition is deferred to a future PR. Either make it return ErrNotImplemented, or land the seal manager first. A stub that lies is worse than a missing method.

issues.description: AdjustErrorStatusCode switch uses errwrap.Contains on error.Error() strings
issues.detail: Refactor preserved the existing pattern of matching errors by substring of their message rather than by identity (errors.Is). This complects error identity with its English rendering — rename ErrSealed's message and routing silently breaks. Not introduced here, but the refactor was a chance to switch to errors.Is for the sentinel cases and was passed over.

Encoding a token as 'TokenLen + literal-dot-byte + nsID' braids three concerns into one string: token bytes, a delimiter, and a namespace identity. A small struct {Token, NamespaceID string} kept as a value through the call chain, serialized only at the wire edge, would let the rest of the code stop parsing. The string format is the easy choice; the value is the simple one.

issues.description: Tests now thread namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) through every call — the context is doing identity work
issues.detail: Dozens of test sites changed from context.Background() to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()). The namespace is a fact about the request, not a property of cancellation; smuggling it through context.Value couples request identity to Go's cancellation plumbing. The fix isn't in this PR, but the churn here is evidence that the namespace belongs in an explicit Request value, not in ctx.

review.summary: The PR is a careful, mechanical extension of root-policy semantics from a single namespace to an ancestry-scoped one, and most diffs are decomplecting in spirit — removing the special-case namespaceMountEntryView, unifying the BarrierView construction through NamespaceView, replacing branchy view selection with one path. That work is SIMPLE in the right direction. The ACL.root field, however, went from a bool to a *Namespace that now carries presence, ownership, and ancestry-check semantics in one pointer — COMPLECTED, and worth naming as a small value type. The NamespaceSealed stub is the larger concern: it ships a method whose answer is always false with a TODO, and ListAllNamespaces now depends on it; the time semantics of 'sealed' are undefined until a later PR lands. The response_util refactor and the test-wide namespace-in-context churn are EASY-NOT-SIMPLE choices the team has already made elsewhere — flagged as P2, not as blockers for this PR.
